haiku-low.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If never claimed, a sweeper runs every minute, marks it EXPIRED, and returns the stock to sale.
haiku-low.q2: Before the charge. If any line is short, nothing is held, Payment is never contacted, and Order replies with the short items (REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK).
haiku-low.q3: The order id is the provider idempotency key and Payment keeps one payment row per order id, so a retried charge cannot charge twice.
haiku-low.q4: Inventory replies STOCK_GONE, the whole order is CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, a full refund is requested, and the customer is emailed. Cart is unchanged.
haiku-low.q5: Cart is emptied when it receives OrderConfirmed, after the stock claim succeeds. If checkout fails, the cart is left untouched.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service moves the checkout through its statuses. Its order record holds the status, such as PENDING or AWAITING_PAYMENT.
haiku-low.q7: The provider calls Payment's webhook. Payment checks it and emits PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined as a broker event that Order consumes.
haiku-low.q8: Payment's webhook log has a unique constraint on the provider event id, so a seen event gets a 200 reply and is ignored. Consumers also ignore repeat events.
haiku-low.q9: Order receives PaymentDeclined, sets PAYMENT_DECLINED, and emits ReleaseStock. Inventory then releases the hold early (RELEASED).
haiku-low.q10: At claim time, if the hold is still HELD it is claimed. If lapsed, Inventory claims only if every line is still free now; otherwise STOCK_GONE and full refund.
haiku-low.q11: The refund becomes RETRYING with attempt count and next try time, and a retry job repeats it with growing delays. It is tracked in Payment's refund row, never dropped.
haiku-low.q12: Order's OrderConfirmed event causes the Cart service to empty the cart. The document says this is the only place the cart is emptied.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If not claimed, a sweeper (runs every minute) marks it EXPIRED and the stock goes back on sale. (A late payment can still claim it if every line is still free.)
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge. If any line is short, nothing is held (all or none), Inventory returns the short items, Order becomes REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK and replies listing them, and Payment is never contacted.
sonnet.q3: The order id is used as the idempotency key on the provider charge, and the payment row is unique on order id, so retries or redelivered PaymentRequested cannot charge twice.
sonnet.q4: Inventory replies STOCK_GONE; Order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, emits RefundRequested for the full amount, and emails the customer. The customer is fully refunded and the whole order is cancelled.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only when the order is confirmed (on OrderConfirmed). On any failure (short stock, decline, out-of-stock cancellation, refund failure) the cart is left untouched.
sonnet.q6: NOT STATED as a single coordinator. Steps are driven by HTTP calls and broker events between services (Order makes the calls and emits events). The order's progress is recorded as the status on the order in Order's database.
sonnet.q7: The provider calls a webhook on Payment (or the watchdog polls the provider after 45 min). Payment saves the result and emits PaymentSucceeded/PaymentDeclined on the broker, which Order consumes and then acts on (claims stock via HTTP).
sonnet.q8: Webhooks: signature check plus provider event id looked up in the webhook log (unique constraint); a seen event gets 200 and nothing else. Broker events: every consumer ignores repeats by event id or order id (e.g. Cart keeps a list of order ids already used to clear a cart; repeated OrderConfirmed has no effect).
sonnet.q9: The hold is released early (RELEASED) and the stock goes back on sale. Triggered by Order, on PaymentDeclined, setting PAYMENT_DECLINED and emitting ReleaseStock, which Inventory consumes.
sonnet.q10: On the claim, Inventory tries once to take the same quantities again, all lines together. If all are still free, it claims late and the order is confirmed; if any line was sold, it replies STOCK_GONE and the order is cancelled with a full refund.
sonnet.q11: The refund is saved as PENDING before the call; on failure it becomes RETRYING and a retry job repeats with growing delays. After N attempts an ops alert is raised but it keeps retrying and is never deleted before COMPLETED. It is tracked in Payment's refund row (order id, amount, status, attempt count, next try time).
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, emitted by Order after a successful claim, causes the Cart service to empty the cart. Cart does it, and it is the only place the cart is emptied.
